title: The Cold room in winter
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：cold　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cold 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the clerk wrote of ① a cold room in winter in the file, and everybody in the office said at once that it was ② colder than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the clerk, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the cold ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the coldest room in winter anybody in the office had ever seen, or so the file for May 1956 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too cold to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the applicant who had come to help; the cold ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a cold reply to the letter, and said that no applicant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as cold as the reply to the letter they had once had in the old office. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was cold or not, and he said so.

By 1969 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the file. What the line asked for was ⑦ something cold, and nothing besides. The applicant from the next office called the whole plan ⑧ quite cold; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the file kept the names of the cold ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1972, on the same day, she wrote of another cold room in winter in the same file, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ colder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The coldest reply to the letter in the whole office, she said in 1974, was the one she could never quite name; the cold ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 寒冷（前置定语 a cold room in winter：1962 年书记员在卷宗里记下的那件寒冷的房间）
B. adj. 寒冷／冷淡（比较级 colder than：文中两处，一处比冬天的房间，一处比预想）
C. adj. 寒冷／冷淡（最高级 the coldest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 寒冷（表语 too cold to do：母亲觉得它太寒冷，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 冷淡（前置定语 a cold reply to the letter：叔叔把整件事称作一桩冷淡的回信里的冷淡）
F. adj. 冷淡（同级比较 as cold as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩回信里的冷淡相比）
G. adj. 冷淡（后置定语 something cold：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 冷淡（受程度副词修饰 quite cold：那位申请人的评价）

items.q: the coldest room in winter anybody
a cold reply to the letter
The coldest reply to the letter in

answers.why: cold 意为“寒冷”，1962 年书记员在卷宗里记下的是“一件寒冷的房间”，此处作前置定语 a cold room in winter。
cold 意为“寒冷”，此处用比较级 colder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
cold 意为“寒冷”，卷宗上 五月 那行字说它是办事处里最寒冷的一件，故用最高级 the coldest room in winter。
cold 意为“寒冷”，母亲认为这件东西“太寒冷了，谁也用不上”，too cold to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
cold 意为“冷淡”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩冷淡的回信里的冷淡”，此处作前置定语 a cold reply to the letter。
cold 意为“冷淡”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩回信里的冷淡一样冷淡”，同级比较用 as cold as。
cold 意为“冷淡”，卷宗上那半行字要的是“冷淡的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something cold。
cold 意为“冷淡”，邻办事处来的那位申请人认为这套计划“相当冷淡”，quite 修饰原级 cold。
cold 意为“冷淡”，1972 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要冷淡”，故用比较级 colder than。
cold 意为“冷淡”，母亲 1974 年说的是“整个办事处里最冷淡的那一桩”，故用最高级 the coldest reply to the letter。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1962 年，书记员在卷宗里记下了一件寒冷的房间。（a cold room in winter）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更寒冷。（colder than …）
母亲觉得它太寒冷，谁也用不上。（too cold to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩冷淡的回信里的冷淡。（a cold reply to the letter）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩回信里的冷淡一样冷淡。（as cold as …）
到了 1969 年，卷宗上只剩半行字：要的是一件冷淡的东西。（something cold）
answers: In 1962 the clerk wrote of a cold room in winter in the file.
Everybody said it was colder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too cold to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a cold reply to the letter.
He said nobody would call it as cold as the reply to the letter they had once had.
By 1969 the file asked for nothing but something cold.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 cold 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1962 the clerk wrote of a cold room in winter in the file, and nobody forgot it.
It was the coldest room in winter in the office, or so the file says.
My mother thought it too cold to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a cold reply to the letter, and nobody argued with him.
The applicant from the next office called the plan quite cold, and everybody laughed.
The cold ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
